Diego / Maya — quick update from infra: we see a sustained burst of small, high-concurrency requests from multiple endpoints for KiteHealth that started ~08:50 PT. Observations:

- Multiple worker GPUs in the Dedicated pool entered a drain sequence due to preemptible scheduling on the underlying host (legacy AWS spot reclamations triggered eviction windows).
- Autoscaler reacted but there was ~4–6 minute lag because the normal scale-up path waits for capacity handshake with the device allocator; when several nodes drain simultaneously, the allocator queues requests causing backpressure and token timeouts.
- Error profile: transient 429s during queue saturation, and 502/504 as RPCs timed out when queued requests hit retry loops. We also saw a spike in client-side retries which amplified load (retry storm).

Immediate mitigations we executed at 09:35 PT:
- Bypassed allocator handshake for KiteHealth for two high-priority slices and provisioned two spare GPU instances from reservoir capacity (manual burst).
- Applied a 10s circuit-breaker in the fronting proxy for KiteHealth to shed retries and reduce queue depth.
- Enabled temporary passthrough routing to Hosted pool for non-sensitive routes (token-verified) to offload lighter requests.

Impact after mitigations: error rate fell ~70% within 4 minutes, latencies returning toward baseline but a small tail remains. We'll hold burst capacity while we run the root-cause analysis.

Logs attached: autoscale-log-20261120.txt; snapshot metric image attached: rbw_instance_metrics.png
